title: Ask Perion brings smarter, faster planning to NZ’s DOOH
summary: Perion’s new agentic AI planner aims to help advertisers and agencies turn marketing briefs into client-ready media plans.
body_markdown:
***[Perion](https://stoppress.co.nz/tag/hivestack/)** ’s new agentic AI planner helps advertisers and agencies turn marketing briefs into client-ready media plans. It cuts the time from brief to decision to execution.*


---


Media planning involves more than understanding the data. It requires translating client briefs into media plans and adapting to changing objectives without getting bogged down in manual processes.


Perion is addressing this challenge with Ask Perion, a self-serve agentic AI interface within Perion One, its AI-native platform for omnichannel advertising execution. Available via desktop and mobile, Ask Perion helps media professionals turn marketing briefs into structured, client-ready media plans.


As digital becomes increasingly central to the market, Ask Perion offers a new way for agencies and advertisers to approach the work behind their campaigns.


## **From brief to client-ready plan**


At the centre of Ask Perion is the Planning Agent, a specialised AI agent designed to simplify media planning.


The Planning Agent tackles one of the most time-intensive tasks in the workflow: translating a marketing brief into a structured, client-ready cross-channel media plan built around the campaign’s goals.


By streamlining this process, it helps reduce the manual work and internal back-and-forth involved in developing recommendations.


That means teams can spend less time gathering and organising information and more time applying their expertise to client objectives.


## **A smarter approach to New Zealand’s DOOH market**


With **[DOOH](https://stoppress.co.nz/stoppress-exclusives/perion-2026-dooh-trends-point-to-a-smarter-greener-and-more-connected-future/)** representing more than three-quarters of New Zealand’s reported **[OOH](https://stoppress.co.nz/tag/out-of-home/)** member revenue, efficient planning is increasingly important.


Digital screens give advertisers the flexibility to tailor campaigns around location, time of day and audience context. Programmatic capabilities add further opportunities to plan and deliver campaigns with greater precision. But making the most of these capabilities requires teams to turn information into decisions efficiently.


Ask Perion is designed to make that process more accessible. By simplifying how teams turn briefs into media plans, it can help reduce operational complexity and support more responsive planning.


For agencies balancing multiple clients, campaign objectives and media opportunities, that means less time spent assembling information and more time evaluating strategies, refining recommendations and identifying opportunities to improve campaign performance.


The mobile app extends this access beyond the desktop, allowing media professionals to progress briefs and plans while working across different locations and priorities.


## **Keeping people at the centre of planning**


While AI can accelerate media planning, strategic judgement remains essential.


Understanding a client’s business, defining success and identifying the right media opportunities require experience and context. Ask Perion is designed to support these decisions by reducing the operational work that sits between a brief and a client-ready plan, not by replacing the expertise behind effective media planning.


It also represents the first phase of a fully self-serve execution model within Perion One, reflecting a broader shift towards more connected advertising workflows.


For New Zealand’s DOOH industry, the opportunity extends beyond the technology itself. As digital advertising evolves, the ability to connect data, planning and execution more efficiently will become an increasingly important part of delivering effective campaigns.


Ask Perion brings these capabilities closer together, helping teams move from brief to plan to decision with less manual effort.
